input.task: What does the catalogue row for the Meridian Wall Clock say?

provenance: the mutation that does NOT end in a recovery, committed with the wrong answer as its expectation because that is what the run really produces. `index` is not a locator tier but it is load-bearing: two of the three live domains reach their answer by counting (live-books-travel-price index 5, live-hn-item1-title index 11), and both cases already declare in their own triage that a re-ordered page would silently return the wrong element. element-reordered is that declaration made executable. Base order is lamp-std, lamp-pro, clock, rug; reversed it is rug, clock, lamp-pro, lamp-std, so `index: 2` moves from the Meridian row to the Aurora Pro row. Nothing catches it: `relocation_candidates` returns no rungs for a target that names no string (deliberate — resolver.py), and BOTH identity-anchor checks pass, because 'Meridian Wall Clock' is on the page whatever row was read. The pair to this case is l4-shop-element-reordered-near, where the same task expressed with `near:` survives the same mutation.

triage.note: support-matrix D5. `mutation_survived: false` keeps this case out of the mutation-survival metric (the only case that still needs the key — every other non-survivor is excluded by its status), and `answer_is_known_wrong: true` makes the published report say that this case's green `answer_matches` is a wrong answer pinned as ground truth: it matches its expectation, and the agent still got the task wrong. Do not 'fix' this case by re-writing the plan to use a name — the whole point is the positional plan.
triage.what_would_catch_it: an identity anchor scoped to the extracted ELEMENT rather than the page — which would break every case whose anchor is legitimately elsewhere on the page (live-hn-item1-title anchors on the submitter while extracting the title), so it is not a fix, it is a different contract. Ground-truth L2 catches it; a live run has no ground truth.
